name: Paradip Port
lat_lon_provenance: Approximate harbour-level coordinate for map display only — not a surveyed berth position.
berth_reference: Kalinga International Coal Terminal (KICT) — Paradip's dedicated coal-IMPORT terminal, commenced operations January 2022, 12 MMTPA capacity, confirmed Capesize-capable up to 165,000 DWT. Draft 17.1m confirmed independently by a CareRatings credit-rating report on the port and by the terminal operator's own page. LOA/beam (290m/45m) are inferred from the stated 165,000 DWT Capesize class capability, not an independently sourced berth dimension — flag if a more precise official berth-table figure surfaces later.
source: CareRatings credit rating report on Paradip Port (port-level draft); Bothra Group (KICT terminal operator) capability page

name: Gangavaram Port
lat_lon_provenance: Approximate harbour-level coordinate for map display only — not a surveyed berth position.
berth_reference: Adani Gangavaram Port's own 2022-23 Berthing Policy & Tariff Structure: coal-priority Berths 5 & 6 both permit 18.0m draft; LOA 292m at Berth 5, 300m at Berth 6 (the more permissive figure is used here). Beam is not published in that document — 48m used here as an engineering inference for a vessel in the port's own stated 'fully laden Capesize up to 200,000 DWT' capability class, not an independently sourced berth dimension. Two mechanized coal berths, 20 MTPA combined coal capacity.
source: Adani Gangavaram Port — 2022-23 Berthing Policy & Tariff Structure (official coal-berth draft/LOA figures); Wikipedia (coordinates, total capacity)

name: Krishnapatnam Port
lat_lon_provenance: Approximate harbour-level coordinate for map display only — not a surveyed berth position.
berth_reference: 18.5m current operational draft (Global Energy Monitor, citing 2023 figures), corroborated by a 2012 dredging-completion record confirming 18.0m (Dredging Today) — one of only three Indian ports, with Mundra and Gangavaram, equipped to receive Capesize vessels; 10 dedicated coal berths added in its Phase II expansion, 41 million tonnes of coal handled in 2018-19. LOA/beam are not independently sourced for this port — 300m/48m used here as an engineering inference for a Capesize-class vessel, the same inference basis used at Gangavaram, not an independently sourced berth dimension.
source: Global Energy Monitor port profile; Dredging Today (2012 draft-completion record); Adani Ports (Capesize capability)

name: Haldia Dock Complex
lat_lon_provenance: Approximate town-level coordinate for map display only — not a surveyed berth position.
berth_reference: Kolkata Port Trust's Haldia Dock Complex — a shallow, tidal-dependent facility, not comparable to the other East Coast ports in this dataset. 9.1m is the maximum tidal-supported draft (Wikipedia, citing official Haldia figures); the average approach-channel draft is only 8.2-8.6m. Haldia 'mainly handles fully loaded Handysize carriers of 28,000-40,000 DWT' at real-world drafts below that max, and Panamax vessels up to 230m LOA only at 40-50% of capacity (partial loading — not modeled by this app's compatibility engine, which only checks full-DWT figures). LOA 240m / beam 32.26m are berths 2, 3 & 4A's own published limits (Berth 4A is Haldia's dedicated coal berth) per a shipping agent's Haldia general-info reference; other berths are slightly smaller at 236m LOA. Given this app's binary, full-draft compatibility gate (no partial-loading model), every vessel class in this dataset is expected to fail here on draft — a real, documented limitation of Haldia's channel, not a modeling bug.
source: Wikipedia (Haldia Dock Complex — draft, tidal, and vessel-size figures citing Kolkata Port Trust); Haldia Dock Complex general-info reference (LOA/beam)
